newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Credit says to deny rumours in briefing.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Credit says to deny rumours in briefing.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd said on Wednesday it will hold an emergency news conference at 5 p.m. (0800 GMT) to deny recent rumours in the Tokyo financial markets.
NCB officials said that vice president Shoji Nishikawa would brief the media. The officials did not specify which particular rumours would be denied.
Earlier, senior managing director Tadao Iwaki was quoted as saying that the bank's financial health was steadily recovering and its profitability was also improving.

Iwaki was quoted by a bank spokesman as saying that the bank was taking serious note of the stock market's view of its share price and would continue to improve its operations in order to win the understanding of shareholders.
That spokesman had also denied rumours that the bank was planning to hold an emergency news conference and that the bank would be involved in a merger.
The rumours had pushed up Japanese government bond prices on Wednesday morning and triggered selling of NCB stocks.
NCB's share price fell to its lowest level for the current financial year, closing down 35 yen at 181 yen. The shares' previous 1996/97 low was 210 yen marked on January 29, 1997.
